request.spec:
Each person's row has a grade select and a save button that records the chosen grade from the
sheet's today exactly as the person form would (PERSON_EDITED and the rollup lines).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Each person's row has a grade select and a save button that records the chosen grade from the
sheet's today exactly as the person form would (PERSON_EDITED and the rollup lines).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I've added the per-row grade select and save button. Two of the four e2e tests pass. The other two fail at steps that don't involve the grade control and that I don't think can pass as the spec is written.

**What I added**
- **Server:** a new endpoint `PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/grade` (`src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/grade.PUT.yml`). It turns the row's grade into a person-form edit (`BuildInlineGradeEdit`) and then runs the form's own save, audit and rollup steps. So it writes the same `PERSON_EDITED` line and rollup lines, takes the grade from the sheet's today, and keeps the name, terms, contact and tags.
  - It sends the version the row shows, so if someone else saved the person in the meantime it is refused.
  - A save from the row also makes another user's already-open person form refuse to save, which the test checks.
  - Viewers are refused by the existing viewer filter, and anything other than A, B or C is refused before anything is written.
- **Front end:** `features/people/inlinegrade.slot.tsx` puts the `person-inline-grade` select (A/B/C) and the `person-inline-grade-save` button on each row. A refusal shows in the row's shared `person-error`, which clears when the select changes or another row action is taken. After a save it reloads the people, claims and pools.

**Test results** (`PORT=3017 bin/e2e`): "inline grade" and "scenario 3" pass. I had to use port 3017 because servers from other sandboxes already hold ports 3002–3004, including the 3002 set in your `PORT`. I didn't touch those processes.

The two failures:
- **Scenario 2, line 603, and also scenario 1, line 207:** the test sets the sheet's parent to `${sheet}-p`, then expects the screen to show the literal text `"__SHEET__-p"`. That looks like a placeholder that was never filled in when the spec was generated. The app correctly shows the real id, e.g. `smvkalmvouzan-p`.
- **Scenario 1, line 152:** this is where scenario 1 actually stops. It expects a statement as of 2026-03-20 to succeed for Eve, who was added when the sheet's today was 2026-04-04. The app deliberately refuses a statement dated before the person was added (`SaveStatement.java`), and the same test expects that refusal three lines earlier for 2026-03-01.

I left both alone because I'm not allowed to edit the spec and they aren't part of this change. Fixing them would mean correcting the spec, or deciding how statements dated before a person was added should behave.
